transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. Can you start by telling me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Well, thank you for seeing me, Doctor. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. Um, I guess I'm here because... well, things have been a little stressful at my apartment lately. It's probably nothing, and I don't want to sound like a bother, but I'm pretty sure the other people living there are keeping track of when I leave and come back. And, um, I know they've been slipping notes about me to the front office. My case worker and everyone else keeps telling me they're just regular notices taped to the doors, but... I don't know, it just feels like more than that to me. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of thing you need to know.
How long have you been noticing this feeling that your neighbors are watching you and reporting on you—days, weeks, or longer?

Oh, um... well, it's been a little while, I guess. I really hope I don't sound too, you know, crazy saying this. I know it probably sounds like a bit much. But I think I first started noticing the... the watching, and the things with the office, about a year and a month ago? Give or take a little. 

I mean, I try not to make a big fuss about it, I really do. I mostly just keep my head down so I don't cause any trouble for anybody. But yeah, it's been going on for about thirteen months or so. Is that... is that the kind of timeline you were looking for, Doctor?
Aside from feeling watched, have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people don't seem to hear, or seen things that others don't see?

Oh, um... no, no, nothing like that. I really hope I'm not giving the impression that I'm completely losing my mind or anything. I've never heard voices or seen things that aren't there. I know that happens to some people, and I'm sure it's awful, but I don't have that problem. It's just the... the stuff with the neighbors. 

I try to be a good neighbor, I really do. I keep my TV turned down low and I don't have company over, so I don't know why they'd be so focused on me. But no, no voices or visions or anything like that. I hope that's okay to say? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

Before this issue with your neighbors started about a year ago, would you say you've generally been a trusting person throughout your life, or have you always tended to be wary and suspicious of other people's motives, even as a teenager or young adult?

Oh, um... well, I wouldn't say I've always been suspicious. I mean, I hope I haven't been. I've always tried to get along with people, you know? Just keep my head down, do my own thing, try not to bother anybody. 

I guess I've always been a little on the quiet side, maybe kept to myself mostly, even back when I was younger. But I wouldn't call it being wary of people. I just... I like to stay out of the way. I've always tried to be polite and trust people when they give me a reason to. It's just lately, with the apartment stuff, that things feel a little different. Is that... does that answer what you were asking, Doctor? I want to make sure I'm explaining it right.

Aside from this issue with your neighbors, how would you say things are going for you overall—are you able to keep up with work, take care of daily tasks, and maintain relationships with family or friends the way you always have?

Oh, um... well, I try my best to keep up with things. I really do. I don't want to sound like I'm just letting everything fall apart, because I'm not. But... I guess things have been a little bit harder lately. 

I hope you don't think less of me, but I've... I've gotten a little behind on some of my bills, and I might have missed a couple of appointments. It's just... it's hard to keep my days organized right now. And I haven't been going to church or doing my volunteer stuff as much. I just... it's hard to trust regular interactions right now, with everything going on. I don't want to make a bad impression on anyone there, you know? 

I really am trying to get back on track, though. I want to be responsible. Is it... is it normal to struggle with that kind of stuff when you're dealing with what I'm dealing with? I hope I'm not doing too badly.

There are no hallucinations, no history of longstanding pervasive suspiciousness or schizotypal traits predating the delusion, and no evidence of disorganized speech, negative symptoms, or bizarre behavior. This clinical picture is most consistent with delusional disorder, persecutory type (F22).
